IELTS Diagnostic Mock: Listening + Reading JURASSIC ENGLISH ™
3Licensed for one learner, or one tutor with their own students
What you get in this pack
Two full-length papers sat in one session, then a marking sheet that codes every miss, ranks the
codes and names one priority. A score tells you where you are. A diagnosis tells you what to do next.
42 printable
A4
pages
This licensed PDF: the learner papers ﬁrst, then the reader's scripts and the marker's keys, kept apart.
40 Listening
questions
Four original scripts read aloud once by a live reader: a phone booking, a talk, a tutorial discussion and a
lecture, with delivery notes for the reader.
40 Reading
questions
Three original passages, entry to top level, on one 60-minute clock: 9 of the 14 Academic task types.
11 trap
codes
Six for Listening, ﬁve for Reading. Every key line gives the answer, the deciding words and the trap it sets.
1 named
priority
The marking sheet ranks your codes by miss share and writes an L1 to L6 result with one primary
constraint and a re-measure date.
1 next
pack
Each primary constraint points to the exact lesson in the Listening Proﬁler Pack or the Reading Ladder
that ﬁxes it.
Every script, passage, question and key is written by Jurassic English. No recordings, exam-board or
published material are included. Raw scores only: the mock does not convert scores to a band and does not
predict a result.
Licence. Printable edition for one learner with a reading partner, or one tutor with their own students. Practice
material, not an oﬃcial score. No resale, sharing, uploading or redistribution. © 2026–2027 WorldWise
Learning and JurassicEnglish.com.

Goal: The learner sits a full-length Listening paper (4 sections, 40 questions, each script read aloud once) and a
full-length Reading paper (3 passages, 40 questions, 60 minutes), marks both, codes every miss by its trap, and
leaves with ONE named priority and the pack that ﬁxes it.
A
score
tells
you
where
you
are.
A
diagnosis
tells
you
what
to
do
next. This mock gives you both: two raw
scores out of 40, and the one trap that is costing you the most marks.
Who
does
what
Role Who What
they
do
Learner the person taking the mock sits both papers under exam
conditions, then ﬁlls in the marking
sheet with the marker
Reader a tutor, a study partner or anyone with
clear spoken English
reads the four Listening scripts aloud,
once each, from the reader section,
and never shows them to the learner
Marker the reader, a tutor, or the learner after
both papers are ﬁnished
marks from the keys and helps code
every miss
Reading can be done alone. Listening needs a reader: there are no recordings, and the scripts are written to be
read aloud live.
The
session
Part Time Pages
Paper 1 · Listening about 30 minutes of listening, plus 10
minutes to copy answers
Listening Question Paper
Break 5 minutes
Paper 2 · Reading 60 minutes on one clock Reading Question Paper
Paper 3 · Marking and diagnosis about 45 minutes, learner and marker
together
Your Marking Sheet
The
rules
in
one
place
Each Listening script is read once, at a natural pace. No repeats, and no pauses except those written into
the script.
The learner never sees a script or a key before marking.
Listening: write on the question paper as you listen, then copy to the answer sheet in the 10 minutes at the
end.
Reading: one 60-minute clock for all three passages. Write straight onto the answer sheet; there is no extra
transfer time.

Spelling counts, and completion answers must keep to the word limit in the instructions.
Raw
scores
only. This mock does not turn raw scores into a band and does not predict a result. Practice
material, not an oﬃcial score.
The
eleven
trap
codes
Every question in the keys carries one code: the trap that question was built to set. When you miss a question,
you take its code. Count the codes and you have your diagnosis.
Paper Code The
trap
Listening DETAIL a number, spelling, plural or date
heard wrong
Listening BAIT the ﬁrst-mentioned detail taken, when
a later one is the answer
Listening PIVOT missed a reversal: but, actually, no
wait, on second thought
Listening SYNONYM the answer is said in other words; the
wrong option reused the speaker's
words
Listening TONE polite words taken at face value; the
voice said reluctant, doubtful or
lukewarm
Listening SPEAKER the right idea given to the wrong
person, or a back-channel taken as
agreement
Reading WM word match: the option repeats the
passage's words but says something
diﬀerent
Reading PM partial match: half the claim is in the
passage; the other half is not, or the
main point was missed
Reading OP opposite: the passage says the
reverse (a negative, a contrast word, a
reversed cause)
Reading EX extra claim: the answer goes further
than the passage (all, always, most, a
comparison it never makes)
Reading LT lost time: found the right place too
late, or never reached the question

Use the rules in order. The ﬁrst rule that ﬁts gives your primary constraint.
1. Time
ﬁrst. If your Reading LT count (the LT questions you missed, plus every blank and time-out guess) is 4
or
more, your primary constraint is LT. Lost time hides every other trap, so it is ﬁxed ﬁrst.
2. Highest
miss
share. Otherwise, take the code with the highest miss share across both papers, as long as it
has 2
or
more
misses. A tie goes to the code with more misses; if still tied, to the code whose misses sit
later in the paper (Listening Sections 3–4, Reading Passage 3).
3. Spread
thin. If no code has 2 or more misses, your primary constraint is consistency under exam
conditions: see the last row of Your next pack.
Your secondary
constraint is the next code by the same rules. Your usable
strength is the code with the
lowest miss share (a tie goes to the code with more items).
